deviations.reason: The sealed lane's dedicated write front door on 127.0.0.1:10100 was not running when this round began (probe returned no response; http=000), while the shared relay on 10101 was up (http=200). The front door is started by the launcher, so the lane was reachable in principle; the maker did not start it and instead performed the bounded writes directly.
deviations.consequence: The bounded-writer property is NOT delivered by the launcher receipt this round. The write surface is bounded only by the round's declared scope and by the committed diff, not by the sealed lane's enforcement. This is a weaker guarantee than R5R's, where the launcher receipts exist.

deviations.reason: The independent acceptance check was dispatched to an isolated Hermes subagent rather than the CODEX CLI checker lane on the OpenAI OAuth route.
deviations.consequence: Context isolation is real (the checker never saw the maker's reasoning, and re-derived everything from the published bytes), but it is NOT the same independence as a separate model family under a sealed lane with its own CODEX_HOME. The maker cannot sign its own verdict in either case; here the substitute is weaker, not equivalent.
